summary: Dedicated pool hitting throttling due to autoscaler not adding GPUs (eu-west)
description:
Deployment mode: Dedicated.

Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden spike in 429s and queueing latency (p95 > 12s) on their Dedicated endpoint. They have burst traffic and expect autoscaler to add capacity.

Impact:
- 429 (capacity) responses ~15-25% for 40 minutes
- Latency increase across all requests

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: LL-EUW-07
- Region: eu-west

Notes:
- Autoscaler shows desired replicas increasing but no new GPU nodes joining pool
- Suspected cloud quota / node provisioning failure path not surfaced in customer metrics.
comments: 2026-01-20 09:12 UTC (Camila Reyes): Confirmed P1. Pulling fleet events + checking node provisioning errors.
2026-01-20 09:26 UTC (Connor O'Brien): Root issue: GPU node group stuck due to invalid AMI ID in launch template (recent infra change). No new nodes could come up.
2026-01-20 09:38 UTC (Connor O'Brien): Hotfixing launch template + manually scaling node group to +8 GPUs.
2026-01-20 10:05 UTC (Camila Reyes): 429s down to near-zero; latency recovering. Customer notified.
2026-01-21 14:40 UTC (Connor O'Brien): Added alerting for 'desired>ready' with provisioning failure reason; PR in slo-toolkit #442.
2026-01-22 08:15 UTC (Camila Reyes): Customer confirms stable through their traffic peak. Closing.
resolution: Fixed node group launch template (bad AMI reference) and manually scaled Dedicated pool. Added alerts for provisioning failures so autoscaling 'no-op' is visible.
workaround: For future peaks until alerts fully tuned: Support can manually scale the pool and confirm GPU quota health via fleet dashboard.
root_cause: Infra change introduced invalid AMI ID in eu-west GPU launch template; autoscaler could not add capacity despite increased desired replicas.
follow_ups: Add pre-merge validation for AMI IDs in terraform pipeline
Document manual scaling steps in support runbook
Review other regions for similar launch template drift
